claim: Two-hop factual recall goes through an intermediate concept
published: Dallas → Texas → Austin path plus a direct shortcut (Claude 3.5 Haiku)
ours: positive embedding → intermediate → answer path in 3/3 public Gemma-2-2B graphs (Dallas, Oakland, Shanghai)
criterion: path present in all checked graphs
post_hoc: criteria written after three runs had moved this result from 0/3 to 3/3

claim: Multilingual circuits share language-independent features in the middle
published: 20 of 27 features shared across English/French/Chinese; language-specific features early and late (Claude)
ours: feature overlap (Jaccard of the 3 graphs): early 0.06, middle 0.17, late 0.07
criterion: middle-layer overlap higher than both early and late
post_hoc: criteria written after the runs had been seen

claim: Confirmatory: the two-hop path runs through the right intermediate
published: Dallas → Texas → Austin (Claude 3.5 Haiku); the path should not appear for a wrong intermediate
ours: path specific to the intermediate (label-permutation p < 0.05) in 0/3 graphs (p: Dallas 0.122, Oakland 0.574, Shanghai 0.610); paths through wrong intermediates found in 0/9 checks
criterion: specific in all 3 graphs and wrong-intermediate paths in ≤ 1 of 9 (pre-stated 2026-11-28)

claim: Confirmatory: middle-layer overlap is specific to the multilingual graphs
published: language-independent features concentrate in the middle layers (Claude)
ours: middle-band Jaccard: multilingual 0.17 vs unrelated-graph control 0.03 (multilingual early 0.06, late 0.07)
criterion: middle > early and late, and ≥ control middle + 0.05; partial if one holds (pre-stated 2026-11-28)
